root_idea.summary: The root centers on deficiency or injustice in apportionment, especially withholding someone’s due.
root_idea.development: The lexical evidence links a deficient division with depriving a person of a right. The root’s etymological origin is reported as possibly deriving from wāw.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the Quran-attested adjective ضِيزَىٰ.

senses.usage_conditions: Used in the Quranic expression قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزَىٰ, describing an allocation or division as defective and unjust.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deviate from the right course; to act unjustly, wrongfully, injuriously, or tyrannically, especially in judgment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive lexical use, including the construction فِي الْحُكْمِ, “in judgment.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deprive or defraud someone of part or all of a right or due; to refuse or withhold it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive construction governing the person’s right or due.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The unit’s independent meaning of deviating from justice or acting unjustly is represented.
The unit’s construction for depriving or withholding a right is represented.
The Quran-attested adjective is represented with its deficient or unjust-division meaning.
